task.description: Independently validate the ISS-0512 async-sandbox-reachability check design against all 4 acceptance criteria and for implementation-readiness.

result.note: All checks pass. (1) Acceptance criteria: (a) fails-on-reach -> design.md section 4 (resolved graph/algorithm) + section 6.2 steps 4-7 + section 6.4 (mix.exs wiring); (b) anchored-not-prose, with a test -> section 2 (anchor rule) + section 8.1 first bullet (moduledoc-only-mention test case); (c) reaper/template not false-flagged -> section 7 (two independent structural reasons: file-pattern exclusion test/**/*_test.exs vs test/support/*.ex, plus neither file has a use...async:true line even if scanned); (d) catches ISS-0480/0113 reintroduction with regression test -> section 8 in full (8.1 unit classification tests, 8.2 --dir scratch-fixture integration test, plus a real-tree smoke assertion). Traceability table in section 10 maps each criterion correctly. (2) No implementation code found: grepped the design doc for def/defmodule/defp -- the only two hits (lines 169, 176) are inline references quoting real existing code (`defp provisioned_tenant(...)` in secrets_test.exs, and a `grep -rn "def provisioned_tenant!"` command shown as evidence), not new Elixir source. The rest of the doc is regex patterns, prose algorithm steps, a data table, and illustrative CLI/report text -- consistent with CODE-DESIGNER's own constraint. No lib/mix/tasks/letflow.check_async_sandbox_reachability.ex file exists yet (verified with ls), confirming nothing was pre-implemented outside the design doc. (3) Independently re-ran the anchor regex myself against the real tree (grep -rnE with --include='*.exs' test/, recursive, not bash globstar): got exactly 66 matches, matching the design's own re-verification in section 1 (and explaining the discrepancy with ISSUE-FIXER's earlier '60' estimate -- design's count is the more careful, current one). Checked every unanchored 'async: true' hit (95 total via plain grep) against the anchored set: all 29 extra hits are moduledoc/comment prose (e.g. router_test.exs:95 '# This module uses...', schemas_test.exs:10 prose sentence, identity_test.exs:42/44 prose) -- none start with a bare 'use' token, confirming zero false positives for the anchor. Verified no multi-line use-declaration shape exists (grep for 'use X,' with nothing else on the line: zero hits), matching the design's claim in section 2. (4) Read tenant_fixture.ex:220-222 directly: provisioned_tenant!/1's body literally opens with `Sandbox.mode(Letflow.Repo, :auto)` as its unconditional first statement, before any opts are even read -- confirms the design's section 3/4 resolution that detecting a call to provisioned_tenant!/1 alone is sufficient without modeling the second hop to ensure_template!/0. Also read tenant_template.ex:60-90: ensure_template!/0 independently calls Ecto.Adapters.SQL.Sandbox.mode/2 at line 82 with an explicit comment noting provisioned_tenant!/1 already sets :auto and this call is idempotent -- consistent with the design's framing. (5) Read secrets_test.exs:1-50 and webhooks_test.exs in full: both moduledocs discuss provisioned_tenant!/1 and Sandbox.mode(...) in prose (secrets_test.exs lines 12, 21-23, all inside the @moduledoc """...""" span), while the real use Letflow.DataCase, async: true declaration (line 31) and the real Letflow.TenantFixture.provisioned_tenant!( call (line 44, inside defp provisioned_tenant/1, not moduledoc) sit outside that span -- exactly the shape the design's moduledoc-span-tracking (section 3) is built to distinguish. Confirms the design's stated false-positive risk and its resolution are both real and correctly handled. (6) Allowlist verified: names exactly test/letflow/secrets_test.exs and test/letflow/webhooks_test.exs with ISS-0113/ISS-0423 citations, matching the two files independently confirmed as the only async:true+mode/2-reaching files in the tree. mix.exs's real alias chain (grep-verified: letflow.check_toolchain -> letflow.check_requirements_registration -> letflow.check_deferral_staleness -> letflow.lint_handoffs -> format --check-formatted -> compile --warnings-as-errors -> letflow.check.test) exactly matches the design's stated current order and insertion point (after lint_handoffs, before format --check-formatted). (7) lint_handoffs.ex precedent verified real and analogous: grep confirms @grandfathered list, grandfathered?/2, --dir <path> flag (ISS-0440, with guard_empty_scope enforcing non-empty scope on an explicit --dir), and the exact Mix.raise message shape the design mirrors. (8) Section 9's five open questions (multi-line use declarations, bare moduledoc use-example lines, direct ensure_template!/0-only callers, future non-allowlisted mode/2-calling support modules, and whether @verified_safe should mechanically cross-check its citation string) are all narrowly scoped, each with a concrete current-state justification (verified zero real occurrences of the risky shape in this codebase) and a stated one-line remediation path if the assumption ever breaks -- none of these are load-bearing ambiguities that would block correct implementation of the stated scope; they are legitimate, explicitly-bounded future-tightening notes, not silently ignored gaps. (9) Ambiguity/implementability check: the design specifies exact regexes, exact exclusion logic (moduledoc span + # comment line, both algorithmically defined), the exact file-discovery glob, the exact allowlist contents and location (module attribute, data-shape left open as a legitimate implementation choice), the exact wiring point in mix.exs, the exact --dir flag semantics (mirroring an existing, real precedent), the exact failure/success message shape, and a concrete three-layer regression-test plan. An implementer would not need to invent any judgment call the design doesn't already make -- the design is fully implementation-ready with no open ambiguity beyond the deliberately-scoped-out items in section 9.
